notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 65-year-old male admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.48, creatinine 1.04, hemoglobin 15.1, platelets 204, sodium 139, wbc 8.4; vitals dbp 70-75, heart_rate 84-89, map 90-96, o2_flow 0-2, resp_rate 17-21, sbp 131-139, spo2 92-96, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity; Oxygen 2 L/min nasal cannula for comfort
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.08, hemoglobin 14.9, platelets 204, sodium 139, wbc 7.9; vitals dbp 71-75, heart_rate 83-85, map 92-96, o2_flow 0-2, resp_rate 16-18, sbp 131-139, spo2 94-96, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 65-year-old male, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
